original_question: If a and b are distinct positive nonintegers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, must the averages (1/N) Σ f(T^[n^a] x) g(T^[n^b] x) converge almost everywhere to ∫f dµ · ∫g dµ?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.3, Problem 24 (“Pointwise convergence”), with immediate context from Section 6.1 (“Powers of a single transformation”) and Section 6.1.2, Problem 23. Your draft is not aiming at a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 package; in this paper the nearest official formulation is Problem 24. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core statement almost exactly: a and b are distinct positive non-integers; one works with an ergodic system with a single transformation T; the test functions are bounded; the averages are along integer-part fractional powers; the expected limit is the product of the integrals; and the desired mode of convergence is almost everywhere. This is exactly the content and intent of Problem 24 in Section 6.1.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: The system should be written as (X, 𝓧, μ, T), not (X, X, μ, T); earlier in the paper a system is a probability space together with invertible measure-preserving transformation(s). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
It should be stated that T is invertible and measure preserving; the paper’s general framework assumes this. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The functions should be specified as f, g ∈ L∞(μ), i.e. bounded measurable functions, which is the paper’s standing convention in these problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The notation [·] should be made explicit: in this paper bracket notation denotes the integer part. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The limit should be stated explicitly as N → ∞, and the conclusion should say ‘for μ-almost every x ∈ X’. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

To be fully paper-faithful, the question should be identified as belonging to Section 6.1, i.e. the ‘powers of a single transformation’ setting, not commuting transformations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

Nearby context says this is a pointwise variant of the mean-limit identity from Problem 23; that context explains why the target limit is the product of the integrals. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
refined_question: Let a, b ∈ ℝ \ ℤ be distinct positive numbers. Is it true that for every ergodic invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and every f, g ∈ L∞(μ), the averages A_N(x) := (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^{⌊n^a⌋}x) g(T^{⌊n^b⌋}x) converge for μ-almost every x ∈ X as N → ∞, and in fact satisfy A_N(x) → (∫ f dμ)(∫ g dμ)?
justification: Problem 24 in Section 6.1.3 is the paper’s exact official formulation nearest to your draft: it asks for the almost-everywhere convergence to the product of the integrals for bilinear averages along [n^a] and [n^b] with a, b distinct positive non-integers. The subsection setup in Section 6.1 fixes that this is a single-transformation Hardy-sequence problem, and Section 6.1.2 explains that the corresponding mean-limit formula is already known. The nearby remark also states that pointwise convergence is open in all cases when both exponents exceed 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
